---
title: "Introduction"
---

Studyflow is a coordination notation for research: a process standard for the cognitive sciences and adjacent fields, in the same role that BPMN[^bpmn], the standard notation for business processes, plays in business.

[^bpmn]: [BPMN 2.0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BPMN) — Business Process Model and Notation, standardized as ISO/IEC 19510.

*Your tools compute. Studyflow coordinates.* A complete programming model has two parts: a computation model and a coordination model. Ordinary code hides the second one inside call graphs and shared state (ordering, dependencies, what each step hands the next). Studyflow makes coordination first-class so computations stay in the tools built for them (Python, LLM, jsPsych, PsychoPy, a Unity scene), while the notation carries what today lives in glue code, preregistrations, or manuscripts.

<figure class="centered max-w-2xl">
  ![](assets/img/studyflow_example_1.svg)
  <figcaption>
    A studyflow: one study as activities, decisions, events, and data.
  </figcaption>
</figure>

One file is therefore the protocol, the runnable experiment, the analysis, and the publication figure at once -- each a projection of the same file, with no second copy to drift:

- *Protocol*: readable by a colleague, reviewer, or ethics board.
- *Runnable experiment*: the runner app administers it to participants or LLMs.
- *Analysis specification*: the Python runner executes its pipeline.
- *Figure*: an PNG or SVG export packaging editable diagram, semantics, and provenance (not just pixels).
